claim: HA_Desktop_Companion (GamerClassN7, Windows, C#) is a Home Assistant desktop companion built specifically to avoid MQTT, using the native HA API with a long-lived token, inspired by ESPHome's native communication protocol.
stance_target: an MQTT-free native-HA-API architecture is a proven alternative for ha-linux-agent (relevant to users who reject MQTT as 'not a native way to integrate')
scope_conditions: Windows desktop companion; repo README; 85 stars, 7 forks, 209 commits
quoted_support: Cause I don't like existing implementations using MQTT and I took inspiration from awesome ESphome and its native communication protocol to HA and implemented it my own way :)

claim: HA_Desktop_Companion implements a compact sensor set (battery_level, battery_state, is_charging, wifi_ssid, cpu_temp, current_active_window, uptime, camera_in_use, cpu_temperature, free_ram) plus an extensible wmic platform allowing arbitrary WMI queries via configuration.yaml (wmic_path/wmic_selector/value_map), and notifications with images, audio, and send-key emulation.
stance_target: feature benchmark for ha-linux-agent: per-host sensors plus an extensible query-platform mechanism and rich notifications
scope_conditions: Windows; sensor list from README; wmic platform config in HA configuration.yaml; send-key requires 'keys:' in configuration.yaml
quoted_support: Sensors implemented currently: battery_level battery_state is_charging wifi_ssid cpu_temp current_active_window uptime camera_in_use cpu_temperature (only native api supported) free_ram wmic (You can integrate any wmix query syou want :))

claim: HA_Desktop_Companion's README points Linux users to muniter/halinuxcompanion as the Linux counterpart.
stance_target: competitive landscape mapping for ha-linux-agent: halinuxcompanion is the designated Linux option in this ecosystem
